FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Contact: Kenny Markwardt, NRTP Communications Director kenny@sandpointstrength.com (208) 610-2220 Courtesy photos by Emily Strizich Introducing the Northern Rockies Trail Project Protecting access. Building the future. Sandpoint, ID — Trails don’t take care of themselves. Someone has to show up — and often, people do, if they’re invited. The Northern Rockies Trail Project (NRTP) is a new 501(c)(3) nonprofit formed to bring trail users together around a shared goal: keeping public lands accessible, maintained, and healthy through collaboration and hands-on stewardship. NRTP grew out of the stewardship work of Pend Oreille Pedalers (POP), a long-standing Sandpoint nonprofit known for building and maintaining bike trails in the Idaho Panhandle. But as that work expanded, so did a realization. “We were leaving people out of the conversation,” says NRTP board chair Emily Strizich. “We wanted to build a bigger table — one where every trail user has a voice.” That vision became clear during a volunteer day at Hayes Gulch, when a dirt biker looked around at the group and said, “No one’s ever invited us to work together before.” “In that moment, we realized our forests and trail networks are too big to manage in silos,” Strizich says. “If we want real progress, we have to work together.” For too long, public land access has been shaped by conflict: litigation, divided user groups, and lines drawn in the sand. Meanwhile, trails fall into disrepair and historic access routes disappear. NRTP’s approach is simple: collaborate early, build trust, and get work done. “When user groups come together on the front end, land managers get better partners, projects move faster, and there’s less conflict later,” Strizich says. “Everyone benefits — especially the land.”

# Page 2^page=2
The organization focuses on trail maintenance, access improvements, volunteer mobilization, and supporting forest management efforts that help landscapes stay resilient to fire, flooding, and overuse. NRTP works alongside the Idaho Department of Lands, the U.S. Forest Service, and other community partners to support professional trail crews and volunteer stewardship efforts at a time when maintenance backlogs continue to grow across public lands. “Improved access protects wild places in more than one way,” says Strizich. “The more people can get out and experience these places, the more they understand what they’re protecting. Our ‘all lands, all hands’ approach means we stop fighting over access and start working side by side to keep it,” Strizich says. “That’s how we protect access and build a future we’re proud of.” Join Us for National Trails Day NRTP is inviting the public to celebrate National Trails Day on June 6 at Canfield Mountain in Coeur d’Alene with a large collaborative stewardship event bringing together mountain bikers, dirt bikers, hikers, horsemen, hunters, conservation groups, land managers, and volunteers from across the region. The event will include trail projects for all ability levels, coffee and donuts in the morning, and a BBQ afterward — along with a few special guests from the world of public lands and trail stewardship. Community members can RSVP and learn more through the NRTP calendar at: Northern Rockies Trail Project About NRTP The Northern Rockies Trail Project is a nonprofit based in North Idaho dedicated to collaborative trail stewardship and public land access. Its approach brings together diverse trail users, land managers, volunteers, and professional crews to keep trails open and wild places cared for.
